headline_marked: ICT-2 to deliver [[verdict in crimes against humanity case]] against Obaidul Quader and 6 others today
headline: ICT-2 to deliver verdict in crimes against humanity case against Obaidul Quader and 6 others today
summary: The seven absconding accused, including AL General Secretary Obaidul Quader, face charges over atrocities committed during the July 2024 uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 (ICT-2) is set to deliver its verdict today in a crimes against humanity case against Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and six others.
The accused, who are all currently absconding, include former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AL Joint General Secretary Bahauddin Nasim, and Jubo League leaders Parash and Nikhil.
The prosecution alleges that Quader used his position as a cabinet minister and party leader to command law enforcement and armed cadres to violently suppress the 2024 quota reform movement.
According to the prosecution, over 1,400 protesters were killed and more than 25,000 were seriously injured in systematic attacks on civilians.
Other accused include Chhatra League leaders Saddam Hussain and Sheikh Wali Asif Enan, who were accused of coordinating attacks and assembling armed cadres.
The trial, which began on February 17, following an investigation that started on June 18, 2025, saw 29 prosecution witnesses testify.
Closing arguments from both the prosecution and defence were completed between August 4 and August 17.
caption:
Over 1,400 killed and 25,000 injured. Today, the ICT-2 delivers its verdict in the case against Obaidul Quader and six others.

The International Crimes Tribunal-2 (ICT-2) is set to deliver its verdict today in a crimes against humanity case against Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and six others.

The accused, who are all currently absconding, include former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, AL Joint General Secretary Bahauddin Nasim, and Jubo League leaders Parash and Nikhil.

The prosecution alleges that Quader used his position as a cabinet minister and party leader to command law enforcement and armed cadres to violently suppress the 2024 quota reform movement.

According to the prosecution, over 1,400 protesters were killed and more than 25,000 were seriously injured in systematic attacks on civilians.

Other accused include Chhatra League leaders Saddam Hussain and Sheikh Wali Asif Enan, who were accused of coordinating attacks and assembling armed cadres.

The trial, which began on February 17, following an investigation that started on June 18, 2025, saw 29 prosecution witnesses testify.

Closing arguments from both the prosecution and defence were completed between August 4 and August 17.

headline_marked: Mymensingh hospital fire: [[Reports of 6 stampede deaths incorrect]], says commissioner
headline: Mymensingh hospital fire: Reports of 6 stampede deaths incorrect, says commissioner
summary: Divisional Commissioner SM Humayun Kabir Sarkar clarified that no one died in a stampede following a fire at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital.
details: A fire broke out at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital (MMCH) around 6:00 pm on Monday, causing panic among patients and attendants as smoke spread through the building.
The panic led to several people being injured while rushing downstairs, but the Divisional Commissioner has denied reports that six people died in a stampede.
Commissioner SM Humayun Kabir Sarkar stated that the administration verified the casualty lists and found that one person reported as dead was actually alive.
He further clarified that two other individuals had died of natural causes and were brought dead to the hospital, meaning their deaths were unrelated to the fire or any stampede.
Ten units from five fire stations were deployed to the scene and managed to bring the blaze under control by 6:30 pm.
The fire is suspected to have started from an electrical short circuit in a non-operational lift, though a full investigation is underway to determine the exact cause.
caption:
Reports of 6 deaths in a stampede at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital have been debunked by the administration.

A fire broke out at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital (MMCH) around 6:00 pm on Monday, causing panic among patients and attendants as smoke spread through the building.

The panic led to several people being injured while rushing downstairs, but the Divisional Commissioner has denied reports that six people died in a stampede.

Commissioner SM Humayun Kabir Sarkar stated that the administration verified the casualty lists and found that one person reported as dead was actually alive.

He further clarified that two other individuals had died of natural causes and were brought dead to the hospital, meaning their deaths were unrelated to the fire or any stampede.

Ten units from five fire stations were deployed to the scene and managed to bring the blaze under control by 6:30 pm.

The fire is suspected to have started from an electrical short circuit in a non-operational lift, though a full investigation is underway to determine the exact cause.

Source: The Daily Star, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune
